description: osira, Open Source Infrastructure Risk Analytics, is a Python codebase for quantifying the direct and indirect impacts of infrastructure cascading failure, for example from cyber-attacks on electricity assets, aimed at insurance and business continuity analysis. Edward Oughton developed it while at the Cambridge Centre for Risk Studies, the University of Oxford and George Mason University, with funding from UKRI's Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council. The documentation cites a 2019 Risk Analysis paper on stochastic counterfactual risk analysis of cyber-physical attacks on electricity distribution networks and a 2016 paper on integrated infrastructure and cyber resilience. Users set primary and secondary parameters, run the scripts and plot results. It is MIT licensed and free, installs with conda and needs Python 3.7 or later. The documentation is dated 2021, so it counts as inactive under the two-year rule, and the code was not run. Caveats: it has one star on GitHub, and data preparation is left to users. Coverage is generic, since users load their own network data. It suits cascading failure, resilience and cyber exposure studies. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
